skill.displayName: Work Productivity Skillscan Security Workflow Helper

version.changelog:
- Updated documentation: README.md and README.zh-CN.md revised for clarity and information accuracy.
- Improved requirement and planning references in requirement-plan.md.
- Removed skill-card.md to streamline project files.

llm.summary: This is a documentation-only workflow helper with overbroad activation wording but no hidden code, credential access, persistence, or destructive behavior.

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request broad filesystem indexing, network access, credentials, external services, or local mutation authority beyond whatever task the user explicitly asks the agent to perform.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifact contains Markdown instructions, README files, a YAML agent metadata file, and a reference plan; no install scripts, executable files, package installation steps, or obfuscated payloads were found.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The trigger keywords and implicit invocation setting are broad enough to cause accidental activation on unrelated requests, but the activated instructions are advisory workflow steps rather than privileged or destructive actions.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No persistence mechanism, background worker, privilege escalation, scheduled task, session/profile access, or credential handling is described.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill’s stated purpose is to help produce workflows, checklists, analyses, and implementation support for SkillScan-style security and reliability work, and the runtime instructions match that purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you want a general SkillScan-style workflow helper. Be aware it may activate too easily because of broad keywords and implicit invocation, so review routing behavior if your agent environment supports adjusting triggers.
llm.findings: [SQP-1] unexpected: The scanner’s broad-trigger concern is supported by the artifact: keywords such as security, every, must, pass, and before plus allow_implicit_invocation are wider than needed. This is an invocation-quality risk, but it does not by itself make the skill suspicious because the artifact is documentation-only and contains no hidden or high-impact automatic behavior.
